title: Meaning
description: A motivation element recording the interpretation or knowledge that stakeholders attach to a specific concept (a term, data item, artifact, or other architecture element) within a stated context, expressed as an explanatory statement of what the concept signifies rather than as an intent, need, condition, or worth. Use Value instead when the statement expresses how much a concept is worth or how useful it is to a stakeholder (financial, strategic, reputational benefit), not what it signifies. Use Principle instead when the statement is normative, prescribing how systems or decisions should behave, rather than explaining what a concept means. Use Requirement instead when the statement declares a need that a system must realize, including a requirement that a term be interpreted a certain way. Use Assessment instead when the statement is a finding from analysing the current state of affairs (strength, weakness, risk, gap), not the interpretation of a concept.

documentation.description: Free-text statement of the interpretation itself: which concept it applies to, the context or stakeholder group in which the interpretation holds, and the meaning given; set it on every instance, since it is the substance of the element.

x-dr-evidence: a glossary or ubiquitous-language document (e.g. GLOSSARY.md, docs/domain-terms.md) defining business terms as used in a specific bounded context
a docstring or comment on a domain class, enum value, or field explaining the business interpretation of the concept, e.g. 'An "active" customer means one with a purchase in the last 90 days'
a data dictionary or schema description entry (e.g. dbt schema.yml column description, JSON Schema 'description', OpenAPI field description) stating what a field signifies for its consumers
